title: Corso di Italiano — Livello A0 · A1 · A2
shortDescription: The SS Europa classroom course, chapter by chapter: from zero to level A2 with the same lessons, slides and tests as your teacher. With English and Punjabi.
description:
This is the official SS Europa Italian course used in our classes, for learners from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who are going to Italy to work, study or live. You start from zero: Chapters 1–7 take you to level A1 and Chapters 8–12 to level A2.

Each chapter (Capitolo) follows the lessons of the classroom: every 60-minute class is split into three short lessons you can study on your phone, with pictures, audio, grammar tables and exercises. Every word comes with its English and Punjabi meaning, and the slides of each class are attached as PDF. Each chapter ends with a test (pass mark 60%), Chapter 7 with the final A1 test and Chapter 12 with the final A2 test; the written part and the oral interview are done with your teacher.
objectives:
Read and pronounce Italian correctly: the alphabet, C and G, the final accents
Greet people and introduce yourself: name, city, nationality, age and phone number
Fill in a form with your personal details, dates and numbers
Talk about your family, your day, your hobbies and your job
Order at the bar and the restaurant, do the shopping and buy clothes
Get around town, ask for directions and describe your home and the weather
Look for a job and book an appointment on the phone
Tell what you did with the passato prossimo and how things used to be with the imperfetto
Travel by train and plane, check in at a hotel and tell the story of your arrival in Italy
Explain your symptoms to the doctor and buy medicine at the pharmacy
Make comparisons, talk about your plans with the future tense
Manage the post office, the Comune, a job interview and repairs at home (level A2)

blocks.title: Le 21 lettere italiane
blocks.body:
The Italian alphabet has **21 letters**: A B C D E F G H I L M N O P Q R S T U V Z.

The letters **J, K, W, X, Y** are "foreign letters" (lettere straniere). They are used only in foreign words such as *jeans*, *kiwi*, *web*, *taxi*, *yoga*.

The 5 vowels (vocali) are **A, E, I, O, U**. In Italian every vowel is always pronounced, and always in the same way.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: A vowel with an accent at the end of a word (**città, caffè, sì, però, più**) is said **strong and clear**, with the voice on the last syllable. The accent can change the meaning: **si** (oneself) / **sì** (yes).

lessons.title: Lesson 1 · Pronunciation: C and G

lessons.summary: Soft and hard C and G: ciao or casa? gelato or gatto?

blocks.title: La lettera C: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**C** has two sounds:

- **Soft [ch]** like *church* (Punjabi "ch", chachā) before **E** and **I**: **ce, ci** — and **cia, cio, ciu**.
- **Hard [k]** like *cat* (Punjabi "k", kakkā) before **A, O, U**: **ca, co, cu** — and **che, chi** (the H makes it hard).

blocks.title: La lettera G: suono dolce e suono duro
blocks.body:
**G** works the same way:

- **Soft [j]** like *gel* (Punjabi "j", jajjā): **ge, gi** — and **gia, gio, giu**.
- **Hard [g]** like *go* (Punjabi "g", gaggā): **ga, go, gu** — and **ghe, ghi**.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Remember the trick: **H after C or G makes the sound hard** (chiave, spaghetti). **I after C or G makes it soft** (ciao, giorno) and the I is almost not heard.

blocks.title: Il verbo AVERE (to have · H muta!)

blocks.body:
The **H** of *ho, hai, ha* is silent (muta): **ho** sounds like "o", **ha** like "a".

In Italian you **have** years: *Ho 20 anni* = I am 20 (literally "I have 20 years"). Punjabi: *Merī umar 20 sāl hai*.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Never say "Sono 20 anni" — that is wrong. Use **avere**: **Ho 20 anni.**

blocks.title: Maschile (-O) e femminile (-A)
blocks.body:
Every Italian noun is **masculine** or **feminine**.

- **Masculine** nouns usually end in **-O**: libro, quaderno, tavolo (Pulling: akkhar -O nāl khatam hundā hai)
- **Feminine** nouns usually end in **-A**: penna, sedia, lavagna (Istrīling: akkhar -A nāl khatam hundā hai)

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **Un'** with the apostrophe is only for **feminine** words that start with a vowel (un'aula). Masculine words with a vowel take **un** without apostrophe: *un amico, un orologio*.

blocks.title: Orientarsi sulla piantina (the town map)
blocks.body:
On the map: **Corso Italia** goes north–south, **Via Roma** and **Via Verdi** cross it.

- **Dalla stazione al bar:** vai sempre dritto in Corso Italia — il bar è di fronte alla Piazza Centrale.
- **Dove si trova la posta?** La posta è accanto alla banca e di fronte alla farmacia.
- **Dal parco all'ospedale:** attraversa Piazza Centrale, vai in Via Verdi e gira a destra — è lontano dalla stazione.

2. **Studente B guida:** vai sempre dritto, all'incrocio, gira a destra / sinistra, attraversa.

blocks.body:

blocks.body: **Fa** always comes **after** the time: *due giorni **fa***, never ~~fa due giorni~~. **Scorso / scorsa** agrees with the noun: *il mese scors**o**, la settimana scors**a***.

blocks.title: Oggetto: La festa di ieri sera!
blocks.body:
Ciao Giulia! Come stai?

Ti scrivo per raccontarti la festa di mio fratello. Prima io e mia madre abbiamo cucinato tanti piatti buoni. Poi gli ospiti hanno portato una torta al cioccolato e abbiamo bevuto il succo di frutta. Dopo abbiamo ascoltato musica e abbiamo fatto tante foto insieme. Infine mio fratello ha aperto tutti i regali!

E tu cos'hai fatto domenica? Scrivimi presto! Un abbraccio, Jaspreet.
blocks.caption:
Hi Giulia! How are you?

I'm writing to tell you about my brother's party. First my mother and I cooked lots of good dishes. Then the guests brought a chocolate cake and we drank fruit juice. After that we listened to music and took lots of photos together. Finally my brother opened all his presents!

And what did you do on Sunday? Write to me soon! A hug, Jaspreet.

blocks.title: Ripasso lampo
blocks.body:
- **Regolari:** -are → **-ato** · -ere → **-uto** · -ire → **-ito**
- **Irregolari:** fatto, detto, letto, scritto, visto, preso, bevuto, aperto, chiuso, chiesto, risposto
- **Quando:** ieri, l'altro ieri, la settimana scorsa, il mese scorso, due giorni fa
- **Ordine:** prima → poi → dopo → infine
- **Negativo:** *non* + avere + participio

blocks.title: Il mio arrivo in Italia
blocks.body:
Mi chiamo Kamal e sono nato in India. Sono arrivato in Italia tre anni fa, nel mese di ottobre.

Prima sono partito da Nuova Delhi in aereo e sono atterrato a Milano Malpensa. Poi mio fratello è venuto a prendermi in macchina e siamo andati a Mantova.

All'inizio sono stato un po' timido per la lingua, ma oggi ho imparato l'italiano e mi sono integrato bene!
blocks.caption:
My name is Kamal and I was born in India. I arrived in Italy three years ago, in October.

First I left New Delhi by plane and landed at Milano Malpensa. Then my brother came to pick me up by car and we went to Mantova.

At first I was a bit shy because of the language, but today I have learnt Italian and I have settled in well!

blocks.title: La nostra domenica a Verona
blocks.body:
Domenica scorsa io e mia moglie ci siamo svegliati presto e siamo andati in stazione.

Abbiamo comprato due biglietti di andata e ritorno e siamo partiti alle nove. Siamo arrivati a Verona dopo quaranta minuti.

Abbiamo visitato Piazza Bra, abbiamo fatto tante foto e siamo tornati a casa alle sette di sera. Ci siamo divertiti tantissimo!
blocks.caption:
Last Sunday my wife and I woke up early and went to the station.

We bought two return tickets and left at nine. We arrived in Verona after forty minutes.

We visited Piazza Bra, took lots of photos and came back home at seven in the evening. We had a great time!

blocks.title: Ripasso lampo
blocks.body:
- **ESSERE** with movement / change: andare, venire, partire, arrivare, tornare, entrare, uscire, stare, rimanere, nascere
- **Agreement:** -o · -a · -i · -e
- **Test:** che cosa? → avere · dove? → essere
- **Reflexives:** always essere (mi sono svegliato/a)
- **Travel:** biglietteria, binario, andata e ritorno, ritardo, valigia, prenotazione, camera singola / doppia

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 9
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 9 (Lessons 1–4).

- **1. Listening** — sentences and a travel story
- **2. Vocabulary** — station, airport and hotel
- **3. Grammar** — essere with agreement, avere or essere, reflexive verbs in the past
- **4. Writing** — your arrival in Italy or a trip

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.

units.description: The parts of the body and saying what hurts (ho mal di…, mi fa / mi fanno male, ho la febbre), at the doctor's and at the pharmacy (la ricetta, lo sciroppo, le compresse, la pomata), the direct object pronouns lo, la, li, le, and the imperative for advice and instructions — informal (prendi!) and formal (prenda!).
canDo: I can name the main parts of the body
I can say what hurts: ho mal di testa, mi fa male la schiena, mi fanno male le gambe
I can explain my symptoms to the doctor and ask for a prescription
I can buy medicine at the pharmacy and understand how to take it
I can avoid repeating nouns with lo, la, li, le: Prendi lo sciroppo? Sì, lo prendo
I can give advice to a friend (riposa, non uscire!) and understand formal instructions (prenda, firmi qui)

blocks.title: Ricorda
blocks.body:
- **lo** = il / lo (masc. sing.) · **la** = la (fem. sing.)
- **li** = i / gli (masc. pl.) · **le** = le (fem. pl.)

blocks.body:
Quando avevo dieci anni, d'estate andavo sempre in campagna dai miei nonni. La loro casa era grande e aveva tanti alberi da frutto.

La nonna preparava sempre dolci buoni e diceva: «Mangia, che devi crescere!».

La sera faceva fresco, guardavamo le stelle e dormivamo con le finestre aperte. Erano giorni bellissimi!
blocks.caption:
When I was ten, in summer I always went to the countryside to my grandparents'. Their house was big and had lots of fruit trees.

Grandma always made good sweets and said: "Eat, you need to grow!".

In the evening it was cool, we watched the stars and slept with the windows open. They were wonderful days!

blocks.title: Com'era la tua infanzia? Intervista il compagno

- **Rispondi all'imperfetto:** inizia con «Quando ero…» e usa *ero, avevo, abitavo, giocavo, andavo, facevo*.

blocks.title: Ricorda
blocks.body:
- **Imperfetto:** background, habit, description, time, weather, age, feelings — *sempre, di solito, ogni giorno, mentre*
- **Passato prossimo:** a single finished event, a sudden action, an exact duration — *ieri, una volta, all'improvviso, due ore*

"When I lived in India, I lived with my whole big family. Our house was always full of relatives and neighbours."

"Today I live in a small town near Mantova. Here life is quieter and more organised, but in India people had more time to be together."

"The summer weather is as hot as in Punjab, but the Italian winter is much colder!"

blocks.body:

blocks.title: Prova 1 · Le domande dell'esaminatore
blocks.body:
1. Come ti chiami, da dove vieni e dove abiti adesso? (**presente**)
2. Che cosa facevi nel tuo Paese prima di venire in Italia? (**imperfetto**)
3. Quando sei arrivato/a in Italia e cosa hai fatto all'inizio? (**passato prossimo**)
4. Quali progetti hai per il lavoro, lo studio o le vacanze? (**futuro**)

blocks.title: Simulazione a coppie: scegli una carta
blocks.body:
- **Carta A · situazione pratica (Lei formale):** colloquio o ufficio pubblico — usa *vorrei, posso, quindi, perché* e i pronomi indiretti.
- **Carta B · confronto ieri e oggi:** città vs campagna / Paese vs Italia — usa imperfetto, presente e comparativi (*più … di / che, meno … di, -issimo*).

blocks.title: Test finale livello A2
blocks.body:
This is the final test of level A2. It checks everything in Chapters 8–12.

- **1. Listening** — sentences and a story in past, present and future
- **2. Vocabulary** — travel, health, daily life and offices
- **3. Grammar** — the tenses, the pronouns, the imperative and comparisons
- **4. Writing** — my story: yesterday, today and tomorrow

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.
